title: Working at Redwood — roles, career ladders, benefits, hiring & onboarding, and internal tools
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood's core company-handbook topics: what it means to work at Redwood, role families and career ladders, benefits & perks, a high-level hiring and onboarding overview, and the primary internal tools new hires use. It is intended as a single-source reference for new and existing employees and hiring managers.

Audience and ownership
- Audience: all Redwood employees and hiring managers.
- Owner: People Ops (primary).
- Maintainers: People Ops, Engineering Managers, Recruiting, IT.

Table of contents
1) Working at Redwood — culture & expectations
2) Role families and career ladders
3) Benefits and perks (summary & links)
4) Hiring and onboarding overview (process & checklist)
5) Internal tools guide (access, first steps, CLI examples)
6) FAQ and support contacts

1) Working at Redwood — culture & expectations

Intro: Redwood is an engineering-first, production-focused company. We value impact, clear ownership, customer empathy, and operational rigor. Our interview and feedback processes emphasize communication, technical excellence, and collaborative problem solving.

Core expectations (across levels):
- Deliver measurable impact: ship features or infrastructure improvements that move key metrics.
- Communicate clearly: asynchronous updates, RFCs/ADRs, and PR descriptions.
- Mentor and grow others: pair, review, and coach.
- Operate with reliability: follow SLOs, on-call practices, and runbooks.

Working norms:
- Asynchronous-first communication; use Slack for near-real-time and Confluence for permanent docs.
- Default to documentation: PRs should include testing notes and rollout steps.
- Quarterly goals (OKRs) align teams to company priorities.

2) Role families and career ladders

Role families supported at Redwood (high-level): engineering, product, research/applied-ML, platform/infra, SRE/ops, security, design, sales, customer success, people-ops, finance/legal.

Career ladder summary (example for Engineering):
| Level | Title examples | Focus areas | Promotion criteria (high level) |
|---|---:|---|---|
| IC1 | Software Engineer I | Learn the stack, deliver small features | Completes onboarding projects; writes tests; participates in code review |
| IC2 | Software Engineer II | Owns components, reduces tech debt | Independently delivers features; improves test coverage; mentors interns |
| IC3 | Senior Software Engineer | Designs modules, coaches others | Drives design discussions; ships cross-team work; enhances reliability 
| IC4 | Staff Engineer | System-level designs, technical leadership | Leads large projects; shapes architecture; measurable impact on latency/cost |
| IC5 | Principal | Strategy and cross-org influence | Sets long-term technical direction; develops org-level standards |

Promotion process (numbered steps):
1. Candidate prepares a promotion packet (summary, 3-5 impact examples, PRs/ADRs).
2. Manager reviews and nominates.
3. Packet goes to promotion committee; reviewers add notes.
4. Committee decision communicated with calibration and leveling.

Manager responsibilities for ladders:
- Maintain role expectations in 1:1s and performance reviews.
- Provide stretch projects and feedback cycles.

3) Benefits and perks (summary & links)

Health & well-being:
- Medical, dental, vision plans with multiple tiers and HSA options.
- Mental health support: 10 free therapy sessions per year and an employee assistance program.

Time off & leave:
- Generous vacation policy (flexible; manager-approved).
- 12 weeks parental leave (primary), 6 weeks secondary; additional bonding leave.
- Company-wide holidays and discretionary winter holiday week.

Financial & retirement:
- 401(k) with company match up to 4%.
- Equity grants (RSUs) with standard 4-year vesting and 1-year cliff.
- Competitive salary bands; compensation review twice per year for promotions and market adjustments.

Learning & home office:
- $1,200 annual learning stipend.
- $800 one-time home office setup allowance for remote hires; office hot-desks and monthly commuter stipend for on-site employees.

Perks & culture:
- Quarterly team offsites, monthly lunch stipend, discretionary hack weeks.
- Wellness stipend and access to partner discounts.

How to view your benefits: People Ops benefits portal (link in Confluence main nav). For detailed plan documents and summaries, see the Benefits & Enrollment page.

4) Hiring and onboarding overview (process & checklist)

High-level hiring steps (recruiting + hiring manager):
1. Requisition created and approved with hiring template (job family, level, compensation range).
2. Recruiter sources and screens candidates; hiring panel defined.
3. Interview loop executes with standardized scorecards and skills rubric.
4. Offer created by Recruiting + People Ops; manager approves.
5. Candidate signs; People Ops coordinates start date and preboarding.

Onboarding checklist (first 90 days) — owner initials recommended
- Preboarding (People Ops / IT)
  - Create accounts: email, Okta, Slack, Confluence, internal Git.
  - Ship laptop and hardware; confirm courier tracking.
- Day 0-7 (Hiring Manager)
  - Welcome 1:1 and team intro meeting.
  - Assign onboarding buddy and first project.
  - Access training: security, code of conduct, and data handling.
- Week 2-4 (Manager + Buddy)
  - First project delivery: small bug or doc update.
  - Initial performance check-in; clarify 30/60/90 goals.
- Month 3 (Manager)
  - 90-day review: discuss fit, blockers, and development plan.

Sample 30/60/90 template (Bulleted):
- 30 days: Understand product, repo layout, run local stack, complete security training.
- 60 days: Ship a small customer-facing improvement or operational runbook.
- 90 days: Own a feature or component and present work at team demo.

Hiring manager checklist (quick):
- Prepare onboarding plan and first project before start.
- Assign buddy and schedule recurring 1:1s.
- Add new hire to team OKRs and invite to recurring squad meetings.

5) Internal tools guide (access, first steps, CLI examples)

Primary internal tools and purpose:
- Okta — identity and SSO (all core apps). Owner: IT.
- Slack — team communication. Owner: People Ops.
- Confluence — documentation and handbooks. Owner: People Ops.
- GitHub Enterprise — code, PRs, and CI integration. Owner: Eng Infra.
- PagerDuty — on-call and incident notifications. Owner: Eng SRE.
- Looker / Metabase — internal dashboards and billing reports. Owner: Finance + Eng Platform.
- Internal CLI: redwoodctl — used for developer workflows, service status, and internal secrets requests. Owner: Eng Platform.

Access & MFA:
- All employees must enroll in Okta MFA within 48 hours of account activation.
- Hardware MFA (YubiKey) is recommended for employees with elevated privileges.

Quick-start: Git and GitHub
1. Accept GitHub invite from People Ops / Eng Infra.
2. Configure git + ssh keys:
   $ git config --global user.name "Your Name"
   $ git config --global user.email you@redwood.ai
   $ ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "you@redwood.ai"
   $ cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub | pbcopy  # paste into GitHub profile

Using redwoodctl (example flows)
- List services and status:
   $ redwoodctl services list --env prod
- Request a secrets grant (creates PR to secrets-approval queue):
   $ redwoodctl secrets request --service payment-api --duration 4h --reason "debugging customer issue"
- Create a short-lived developer sandbox:
   $ redwoodctl sandbox create --template minimal --expires 24h

Note: redwoodctl requires Okta session or API token. See eng-infra onboarding page for token creation.

Confluence doc templates and where to find them:
- PRD, RFC, ADR, and Postmortem templates live in Confluence: /confluence/templates. Use the PRD template for cross-team feature requests.

Security & data handling reminders:
- Do not copy customer PII into Slack channels. Use secure upload to S3 with proper tagging when required.
- Follow data classification and retention policies in security-and-compliance.

6) FAQ and support contacts

Common questions
- Who do I contact about payroll or benefits? People Ops (people-ops@redwood.ai).
- How do I escalate an urgent access issue? Ping IT in #it-ops and open an Okta ticket.
- How do I request equipment? File a request in the internal IT portal; for urgent needs, email it-fulfillment@redwood.ai.

Escalation paths
- Account or access issues: IT -> People Ops -> Security (if suspect compromise).
- Onboarding blockers (manager or repo access): Hiring manager -> Eng Infra -> Eng Platform.

Governance and updates

Contact
- People Ops (owner): people-ops@redwood.ai
